_comment: Tune here, not in code. Weights are additive points unless noted. Run `python build.py --explain` to see why any item scored what it did.

gate._comment: Permissive by design. An item must hit ONE of these to enter at all. Everything rejected is written to data/filtered.json for review. trusted_sources bypass the keyword gate: these feeds are domain-specific by construction (we only query EDGAR for defence companies; an IR feed carries one company's news), so items like '10-Q Quarterly Report' should not be dropped for lacking generic defence vocabulary. The relevance pass still judges whether each item matters.

magnitude._comment: Dollar figures are parsed from title+summary and log-scaled. A $50B award outranks a $12M SBIR automatically.

entities._comment: Tiered. Highest single hit applies, plus a small bonus per additional distinct entity.

corroboration._comment: Cross-source clustering is the main 'is this big' signal. Points per additional source carrying the same story.

dib_override._comment: The DIB problem: the most valuable industrial-base items are structurally single-source and would be buried by corroboration scoring. If an item hits these terms it gets a floor score regardless of how many outlets carried it.

sections._comment: Router. Each item is assigned to exactly ONE section: the highest-scoring match. Ties broken by 'priority' (lower wins).

recency._comment: News decays faster than analysis so deep-dives persist, but the gap must stay narrow: at 2.5 vs 0.6 a three-day-old essay outranked a fresh programme milestone. analysis_base_points offsets the corroboration bonus analysis can never earn.

clustering._comment: Duplicate detection across sources, inverse-frequency weighted so rare tokens (pac-3, sentinel) count far more than common ones (lockheed, missile). Dollar figures are normalised into a shared token but can never create a match alone. Deliberately biased toward NOT merging: a false split only costs a corroboration bonus, a false merge silently deletes a story. Stable band is 0.45-0.60; 0.50 sits in the middle so corpus shifts don't flip behaviour.

reject._comment: Hard exclusions applied BEFORE the gate. Drops items regardless of keyword hits. URL patterns are far more precise than title keywords - human-interest features live under predictable paths. Rejected items land in data/filtered.json with the reason, so you can audit what was dropped.
summary_terms: only for war on the rocks members

routing._comment: tier1_triad_bonus: points added to triad when a tier-1 entity appears. lock_tier1_to_triad forces NEWS items on those programmes into triad so awards and milestones cannot be claimed by other sections - but it deliberately does NOT apply to analysis, which routes normally so commentary lands in Analysis & Research.

semantic._comment: Model-based relevance for the ambiguous middle. Keyword rules cannot tell a land-based-deterrence essay from a Nicaragua politics essay, or an AI-silicon story from an AI-paperwork story. Only items scoring between floor and ceiling are sent: high scorers already have hard evidence (dollars, corroboration, tier-1 programme), low scorers are noise. Set enabled=false to disable entirely. Without ANTHROPIC_API_KEY it silently no-ops.
semantic.thesis:
You are filtering a news brief for an investor building a HOLDING COMPANY of small private businesses deep in the US defense industrial base - Tier 2 to 4 suppliers of engineered components, specialty processing, and accredited testing, bought and consolidated into a durable platform of strategic assets. The purpose of this brief is twofold: (1) become a subject-matter expert on the industry, and (2) find and evaluate acquisition targets.

Core focus: the US nuclear enterprise (Sentinel, Columbia/Trident, B-21, LRSO, warheads, NNSA sites including Pantex, Y-12 and Kansas City), missiles and energetics, specialty materials (carbon phenolic, ablatives, solid rocket motors, castings, forgings, coatings), rad-hard microelectronics and hi-rel interconnect, and commercial and installation nuclear power as a second end market.

Rate HIGHEST the things that inform buying or valuing a small supplier: qualification barriers and certifications, sole-source and second-source decisions, production capacity and bottlenecks, supplier-base health and consolidation, DPA Title III and industrial base policy, M&A involving sub-tier suppliers and the sponsors doing it, contract awards that signal sustained demand, skilled-labour and workforce constraints, and prime commitments that pull volume through the supply chain.

Rate LOW or ZERO: geopolitics and foreign policy commentary, personnel moves, ceremonies and public affairs, software and IT with no hardware implication, general military operations, equity-market and share-price news, and anything about a company's stock rather than its production.

Calibration notes:
- Threat and capability assessments of peer adversaries are relevance 2, or 3 where they reach conclusions about force structure, weapons inventories or industrial capacity - they are the demand driver behind procurement volumes.
- Other countries' internal politics and third-party diplomacy are relevance 0.
- Cyber requirements flowed DOWN to suppliers (CMMC, NIST 800-171, facility clearances) are relevance 3 and belong in the industrial base section - they are qualification barriers our targets must clear. The Department's own IT is relevance 0.
- Schools, healthcare, personnel policy, facilities management, chemical or border security and disaster response are relevance 0 regardless of which agency published it.
- Summit diplomacy and alliance politics are relevance 0 unless they reach explicit conclusions about force structure, inventories, industrial capacity or procurement.

section_guide.triad: EVENTS in the US nuclear enterprise: Sentinel/ICBM, Columbia/Trident/SLBM, B-21, LRSO, SLCM-N, warheads, NNSA sites (Pantex, Y-12, Kansas City, Los Alamos, Livermore, Savannah River). Production milestones, tests, contract awards, programme decisions, facility news. Commentary and research ABOUT these programmes is analysis, not this section.
section_guide.dib: Industrial base mechanics: supplier capacity, bottlenecks, sole/second sourcing, qualification, energetics and specialty materials, castings and forgings, shipyards and depots, skilled labour, critical minerals, DPA Title III. Also includes compliance and qualification regimes imposed ON suppliers - CMMC, NIST 800-171, NADCAP, AS9100, ITAR registration, facility clearances. Contract awards for components, materials, energetics and capacity belong here.
section_guide.budget: Appropriations, NDAA, reprogramming, acquisition policy and reform, GAO oversight of defence spending, programme cost and schedule baselines.
section_guide.primes: What the PRIMES are doing that implies demand for the tier beneath them: capacity expansions, new facilities, production-rate changes, backlog, supplier investment, make-vs-buy shifts, restructuring that moves work, earnings commentary on throughput or supply constraints. The question is always what this means for sub-tier suppliers, not how the company's stock is doing. NOT contract awards (those go to the subject), NOT M&A (deals), NOT ownership or trading news.
section_guide.deals: Ownership and capital transactions: M&A, take-privates, divestitures, carve-outs, IPOs, antitrust, AND startup funding rounds of any size (seed through late stage). A company raising money belongs here, not in primes.
section_guide.nuclear_energy: US commercial and defence-installation nuclear: reactors, restarts, SMRs and microreactors, fuel cycle and enrichment, utility and hyperscaler power deals, DOE loans, NRC licensing. Foreign reactor construction, foreign utility news and general industry promotion with no US supply-chain or technology link is relevance 0.
section_guide.tech: Enabling HARDWARE and the systems that pull it: rad-hard microelectronics, trusted foundry, packaging, sensors, seekers, power, thermal, autonomy and unmanned platforms, directed energy, space hardware. AI and software only when they drive hardware demand - an AI tool for staff work, chatbot adoption or IT modernisation is relevance 0.
section_guide.global: Defence procurement, industry and military capability of OTHER countries - allies and partners (NATO, AUKUS, Japan, Korea, Israel, Ukraine, Poland, India) and adversaries (Russia, China, Iran, North Korea). Their orders, exports, co-production, FMS, shipyards and production rates. NOT their internal politics, leadership succession, regional diplomacy or third-party disputes - those are irrelevant. If the argument is really about US posture or capability, it is analysis, not this section. A piece whose subject is US policy, US forces or US industry is NOT this section even when it discusses allies - US trade policy toward allies, US naval readiness, US posture in Europe all belong in analysis.
section_guide.thinktank: Strategic analysis, essays and research reports whose argument bears on US capability, posture, force structure, deterrence or what the US should buy - INCLUDING nuclear enterprise commentary (deterrence posture, ICBM force structure, stockpile policy, test and evaluation practice). Adversary assessments and contingency analysis belong here too. Not news reporting, not government announcements, not programme milestones.

awards_strip._comment: Compact scannable list of transactions near the top of the page. Items still live in their subject sections; this is a view, not a section. An item qualifies if it carries award language AND a dollar figure, or is flagged by the semantic pass.

market._comment: Closing prices. Twelve Data (TWELVEDATA_API_KEY) is the working source from CI - Yahoo returns 429 and Stooq serves a bot page to datacenter IPs. FRED (FRED_API_KEY) supplies treasury yields, which are not on equity free tiers. SPY/QQQ stand in for the S&P and Nasdaq indices, since free tiers cover ETFs but not indices. Both keys optional; without them the strip is simply omitted.

email._comment: Newsletter ingestion for sources that block CI (Substack, CSBA, AEI return 403 to datacenter IPs) or have no feed at all (ExchangeMonitor). Read-only IMAP against a dedicated Gmail account. Credentials come from MAIL_USER / MAIL_PASSWORD secrets - Gmail requires an APP PASSWORD with 2FA enabled, not the account password. Match is on the From header, so add a sender entry for each newsletter you subscribe to.

edgar._comment: DISABLED. Built for ownership and control events (SC 13D, S-4), which is trading-adjacent intelligence - not the use case. This brief reads companies for demand signal, capacity moves and comps, and filings do not carry those: the IR feeds do. Kept in the codebase in case a filings need emerges; set enabled=true and pick forms. Requires SEC_USER_AGENT.
